_README.about: Compiler configuration for the detector-construction compiler. Two sections: 'hardware' (the tree of control boards; circuit-agnostic) and 'postselect' (the explicit set of postselect detectors; circuit/decoder-specific). Provide only physical facts + the postselect list; the compiler derives the rest (measurement widths, detector in/out widths, channel placement, stage boards).
_README.name: free-text name of this configuration
_README.hardware.layers: ordered list of board layers; level 0 = leaf layer (wired to qubits), last level = root
_README.hardware.layers[].level: layer index; 0 for the leaf layer, increasing toward the root
_README.hardware.layers[].boards: list of boards in this layer
_README.board_id: globally-unique integer id for the board (unique across ALL layers)
_README.qubits: [leaf, or a monolithic root] every physical qubit index wired to this board (measured or not); the compiler keeps the ones actually measured into detectors
_README.monolithic: a single-board system = ONE layer of type 'root' whose board carries 'qubits' (leaf+root fused): it is wired to qubits AND is the endpoint (no children, no raw_out). Example: hardware.layers=[{level:0,type:'root',boards:[{board_id:0,qubits:[...],kernels:{...}}]}]
_README.children: [router/root only] board_id list of the boards in the previous layer that feed this board
_README.kernels: list of detector channels this board has; length = number of kernels (k)
_README.kernels[].n: selector width: how many measurement lines this kernel may pick from the board's measurements
_README.kernels[].h: number of cores in this kernel = how many detector time-indices it can build in parallel
_README.raw_out: [leaf/router only] max number of raw (unconstructed) measurements this board may forward to its parent; root has none (endpoint)
_README.postselect: WHICH detectors to postselect (fire => discard the shot): 'none' (or []) for codes without postselection, an explicit list of stim detector indices, or {'from_file': <json path>} reading the list from a JSON file (a bare list, or a dict whose 'postselected_detectors' key holds it; override the key via 'key'). Relative paths resolve against this config's directory.
_README.postselect_source: the postselect set is a circuit+decoder property computed by the decoder workflow, not by a coordinate rule in the compiler — for cultivation circuits, algorithms/get_desaturated_dem_with_obs_detector.py writes postselected_detectors.json next to the circuit copy
_README.derived_not_here: m (measurement inputs), detector in/out widths, raw inputs, each router/root's qubit scope, channel->kernel assignment, and per-stage postselect/matchable split are all derived by the compiler
